title: Canonical closed-support kernel functor for condensed module sheaves
statement:
Let $\Lambda$ be a condensed ring, not necessarily commutative [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring]. For each scheme $S$ [def-pc-scheme], put $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients] and $\mathcal M_S=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_S}(\operatorname{Sh}(S_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\mathrm{Ab}))$ [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. For a scheme morphism $f:S\to T$, use the abelian-sheaf inverse and direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], their transport to module objects [sk-def-sfb-transport], and the canonical coefficient isomorphism $\alpha_f:f^*\Lambda_T\simeq\Lambda_S$ and its mate $\eta_f:\Lambda_T\to f_*\Lambda_S$ [sk-def-sfb-coefficient-morphisms]. Define module inverse image by transporting along $f^*$ and restricting scalars along $\alpha_f^{-1}$, and module direct image by transporting along $f_*$ and restricting along $\eta_f$, using [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Write $u_j:\mathrm{id}\to j_*j^*$ for the unit of their canonical module adjunction. For arbitrary scheme morphisms $i:Z\to X$ and $j:U\to X$, define $K_j(M)=\ker(u_{j,M}:M\to j_*j^*M)$ in $\mathcal M_X$, its natural inclusion $\kappa_M:K_j(M)\to M$, and the additive functor
$$\Gamma_{i,j}:\mathcal M_X\longrightarrow\mathcal M_Z,\qquad \Gamma_{i,j}(M)=i^*K_j(M).$$
On a module map $a:M\to N$, $K_j(a)$ is the unique kernel map satisfying $\kappa_N\circ K_j(a)=a\circ\kappa_M$, using naturality of $u_j$, and $\Gamma_{i,j}(a)=i^*K_j(a)$. In particular, for a closed immersion $i$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with complementary open immersion $j$ [def-weil-open-immersion], this defines the closed-support functor $\Gamma_Z(M)=i^*\ker(M\to j_*j^*M)$. The definition uses the actual unit and kernel, with no exceptional adjunction or derived identification chosen as data.
